description: Four random voltage sources stepping to a new value on their own timers: a signed and an unsigned output for each of a left and a right pair

params.text: Sets how long that output holds each value, 50ms at 1 rising to 450ms at 9, so a higher setting changes more slowly
Sets the size of that output's signed values: the knob setting times 0.44 gives the middle of a band a volt either side, and the sign is drawn afresh each time
Sets the size of that output's unsigned values: the band runs from one below the knob setting to one above it, so 0V to 2V at 1 and 8V to 10V at 9; the maker's tooltip calls this control Spread
Sets the hold time for all four outputs while the general switch is on, 50ms at 1 rising to 450ms at 9
Sets the size of the values for all four outputs while the general switch is on; the maker's tooltip calls this control Spread
Puts all four outputs onto the two knobs above it and makes the module draw a single random value for all of them; the eight CV jacks are ignored while it is on

inputs.text: Replaces that output's Freq knob while a cable is here, -5V giving the 50ms setting and +5V the 450ms setting, with anything beyond either end clamped
Replaces the LvL knob for that signed output while a cable is here, -5V giving 0.36 and +5V giving 3.96 as the middle of the band
Replaces the LvL knob for that unsigned output while a cable is here, -5V giving 0.8 and +5V giving 8.8 as the setting the band is built from

outputs.text: A random voltage that can come out positive or negative, replaced by a fresh one each time its own timer comes round
A random positive voltage, replaced by a fresh one each time its own timer comes round

notes: the four Freq knobs in the columns come up at 0, which is below their own range of 1 to 9, so each output draws a new value every sample until its knob is moved.
a CV jack replaces its knob rather than adding to it, and every CV jack is ignored while the general switch is on.
with the general switch on, one random value is drawn each sample; the signed outputs take it as it stands and the unsigned outputs take twice its size.
the timers run on the computer's clock rather than on Rack's sample count, so the hold times do not follow the sample rate.
this module is monophonic: only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read, and each output carries one channel.
